title: 3 numbers for a teen's first Roth
hook: Three numbers decide your teen's first Roth contribution.

concepts.title: Number one: earned income
concepts.body: Number one is earned income. The teen needs to have actually been paid — W-2 wages, tips, or self-employment income. Allowance and investment gains don't count. The Roth contribution can't exceed what the teen actually earned.

concepts.title: Number two: the 2026 limit
concepts.body: Number two is the 2026 limit — seven thousand five hundred dollars. But the contribution can't exceed their earned income. So a sixteen-year-old with a three-thousand-dollar summer job can put in three thousand. Not seven-five. Earned income is the binding cap.

concepts.title: Number three: age 18
concepts.body: Number three is the year they turn eighteen. A custodial Roth — what minors use — converts to a regular Roth on the teen's eighteenth birthday. The five-year clock for tax-free withdrawals of earnings also starts on that date.
